content: Ketoconazole cream is prescribed to treat various fungal skin infections, including tinea corporis (ringworm), which causes a red, scaly rash on different parts of the body; tinea cruris (jock itch), a fungal infection in the groin or buttocks; tinea pedis (athlete's foot), a fungal infection of the skin on the feet and between the toes; tinea versicolor, a fungal infection that results in brown or light-colored spots on the chest, back, arms, legs, or neck; and yeast infections of the skin. Prescription ketoconazole shampoo is used to treat tinea versicolor. Ketoconazole belongs to a class of antifungal medications called imidazoles, which work by slowing the growth of fungi responsible for infections. Prescription ketoconazole is available as a cream and a shampoo for application to the skin. Over-the-counter ketoconazole is available as a shampoo for application to the scalp. The cream is typically applied once daily for 2 to 6 weeks. Prescription shampoo is usually applied once to treat the infection. Over-the-counter shampoo is generally used every 3 to 4 days for up to 8 weeks and then as needed to control dandruff. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use ketoconazole exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed. A single treatment with prescription shampoo may effectively treat tinea versicolor, but it may take several months for your skin color to return to normal, especially if exposed to sunlight. After treatment, there is a possibility of recurrence of tinea versicolor. If using over-the-counter shampoo for dandruff, symptoms should improve within the first 2 to 4 weeks of treatment. Contact your doctor if symptoms do not improve or worsen during treatment. If using the cream, symptoms should improve early in the treatment course. Continue using the cream even if you feel better, as stopping too soon may result in incomplete treatment and symptom recurrence. Ketoconazole cream and shampoos are for external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes or mouth, and do not swallow the medication. If the cream or shampoo gets into your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water. To use the cream, apply enough to cover the affected area and the surrounding skin. For prescription shampoo, follow these steps: 1. Wet the affected skin area with a small amount of water. 2. Apply the shampoo to the affected skin and a large surrounding area. 3. Rub the shampoo with your fingers until it forms a lather. 4. Leave the shampoo on the skin for 5 minutes. 5. Rinse the shampoo off with water. For over-the-counter shampoo, follow these steps: 1. Ensure your scalp is not broken, cut, or irritated. Do not use the shampoo if your scalp is damaged or irritated. 2. Wet your hair thoroughly. 3. Apply the shampoo to your hair. 4. Rub the shampoo with your fingers until it forms a lather. 5. Rinse the shampoo out of your hair with plenty of water. 6. Repeat steps 2–5. Ketoconazole cream and prescription shampoo are sometimes used to treat dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, a condition causing skin flaking. The cream is also occasionally used to treat tinea manuum, a fungal infection of the skin on the hands. Additionally, the cream may be used with other medications to treat skin conditions worsened by fungal infections, such as diaper rash, eczema (skin irritation caused by allergies), impetigo (blisters caused by bacterial infection), and psoriasis (a chronic skin condition). Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Ketoconazole may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using ketoconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ketoconazole or any other medications, creams, or shampoos. If using the cream, notify your doctor if you are allergic to sulfites. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as your doctor may need to adjust dosages or monitor for side effects. Inform your doctor of any medical conditions you have or have had. If using the cream, mention if you have or have had asthma. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using ketoconazole, contact your doctor. Unless instructed otherwise by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ketoconazole may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Changes in hair texture Blisters on the scalp Dry skin Itching Oily or dry hair or scalp Irritation, itching, or stinging at the application site Some side effects may be serious. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Rash Hives Difficulty breathing or swallowing Redness, tenderness, swelling, pain, or warmth at the application site Ketoconazole may cause other side effects. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while using this medication. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store ketoconazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Protect it from light and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. If someone swallows ketoconazole cream or shampoo, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Ketoconazole shampoo may remove curls from permed hair. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If symptoms persist after completing the medication, contact your doctor.
